source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Corvette Body, p.1B-41

procedures.title: Hard top vinyl covering: install
steps: Coat the whole fabric roof cover with cement and let it dry about 15 minutes.
Fold the vinyl cover back onto the cemented roof panel, keeping the cover seam parallel to the car's center line.
Repeat for the other side of the roof.
Work out wrinkles and bubbles with a spatula or roller.
Trim the extra vinyl all around the top, leaving a flange of at least 1/2" to cement to the removable hardtop substructure.
Reinstall the reveal moldings and weatherstrips.

procedures.title: Vinyl roof cover: repair scuffs or small cuts near exterior moldings
steps: If there is a small cut, first try to cement the loose ends.
Get scrap roof cover material, or take some from a hidden spot on the same car (e.g. under the reveal moldings).
With an electric wood-burning needle or low-heat soldering gun, scrape vinyl off the scrap or hidden area and apply it at once to the damaged spot.
Blend the added vinyl into the cover with the needle or soldering gun.
notes: These repairs avoid removing or replacing the cover.
Caution: keep the heat low or the cover can discolor.

procedures.title: Vinyl roof cover: repair wrinkles, blisters and bubbles
steps: Prick every wrinkle, blister and bubble with a small needle.
Soak a clean shop towel in water and wring it out.
Lay the towel over the affected area.
Run a household iron back and forth over the towel until it is dry; if the iron has settings, use "wool".
Remove the towel and check the area.
If slight wrinkles or blisters remain, use a syringe with a hypodermic needle to inject enough clear water to dampen the fabric backing.
Then repeat the towel and iron steps (steps 2 through 4).
notes: Caution: stop ironing once the towel is dry; extra heat can permanently damage the vinyl cover.

procedures.title: Folding top: care
steps: Do not leave the top folded for long if it is damp or soaked; let it dry in the raised position before stowing.
Do not put advertising stickers, gummed labels or masking tape on the plastic back window.
notes: Storing a wet top folded risks water stains, mildew or shrinkage.
Sticker adhesive is hard to remove and may harm the plastic window.

procedures.title: Folding top plastic rear window: care and cleaning
steps: For light dust, never use a dry cloth; wipe across the window with a soft cotton cloth dampened with water.
To wash, use cold or tepid (not hot) water with mild neutral soap suds, rinse with clear water, and wipe with a slightly damp clean soft cloth.
Do not scrape off frost, snow or ice; in an emergency warm water may be used, keeping it off the glass windows and windshield.
notes: The plastic scratches and abrades easily.
A quality plastic window cleaner is sold through Chevrolet parts sources.
Caution: never use alcohol or other solvents or volatile cleaners on the plastic window; they can deteriorate it, and spills can spot the paint on the rear body panels below.

procedures.title: Folding top: adjustments
steps: Top fit is adjusted at 3 locations (see figure 70 in the manual); a mix of these, plus door and window adjustments, may be needed.
Header: remove the header trim panel, loosen the 2 clamping screws and move the header fore or aft.
To reach the outer header clamping screw, remove the side roof rail weatherstrip (see Weatherstrip).
Hinge: remove the rigid plastic trim (see Interior Trim) to reach the hinge.
Move the hinge up/down and fore/aft within the slotted holes in the hinge plate and body.
notes: Header adjustment fixes header latch guide pin alignment with the windshield upper frame holes; signs of misalignment are loose top trim when up and locked, and hard-to-engage header locks.
